chunks: And the people of Moses took (for worship) from after him (his absence) from their ornaments a calf which had a lowing sound. Did they not see that it could neither speak to them nor guide them to a path? They took it (as a deity), and they were wrongdoers.
ai.seo_question: What did the people of Moses worship in his absence and why was it significant?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the concept of *al-‘Ajl* (the calf) as a symbol of hasty, superficial worship (*‘ibadat al-jahil*) that lacks the capacity for divine guidance (*huda*). The phrase 'a body having a lowing sound' (*jasadan lahu khwarun*) is interpreted by scholars like Al-Tabarsi to highlight the absurdity of attributing divinity to an inanimate object that cannot even communicate, thereby emphasizing the injustice (*dhulm*) of the Israelites in turning away from the true God. This incident serves as a cautionary archetype for the Shia tradition regarding the distinction between true spiritual insight and mere ritualistic conformity.
